Here’s a structured 12-week hypertrophy program for a 26-year-old intermediate lifter with full gym access. It’s designed around progressive volume and intensity, strategic variation, and built-in deloads to manage fatigue. Split evolves across phases to keep stimulus novel while emphasizing the big rocks: sufficient volume, mechanical tension, and proximity to failure.

Overview
- Frequency: 5 days/week
- Primary Goal: Hypertrophy with progressive overload
- Intensity guideline: Most working sets 1–3 reps in reserve (RIR), occasionally to 0–1 RIR on last set of key compounds.
- Progression: Add load when you hit top of rep range on all sets with good form, or add 1–2 reps per set until cap, then load.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3s), explosive but controlled concentrics.
- Rest: 2–3 min compounds, 60–90s isolations.
- Warm-up: 5–10 min light cardio + dynamic mobility + 2–3 ramp-up sets for first two lifts.
- Deloads: Week 4 and Week 8 are deloads (reduced volume/intensity).

Phases
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation Volume and Technique—Upper/Lower split (4 days) + optional pump day (1 day). Accumulate volume, prime movements. Deload in Week 4.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensified Volume—Push/Pull/Legs/Upper/Lower (5 days). Slightly higher intensity, introduce variants to change strength curves. Deload in Week 8.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Advanced Hypertrophy—Upper/Lower/Push/Pull/Legs (5 days) with strategic intensification techniques on final sets.

Weekly Structure by Phase

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Upper/Lower + Optional Pump)
- Days: U/L/U/L + optional Pump/Arms/Delts
- Weekly target sets per muscle (wk1): quads 12–14, hams 10–12, glutes 10–12, chest 12–14, back 14–16, delts 10–12, biceps 8–10, triceps 8–10, calves 8–10, abs 6–8.

Daily Session Template (apply each day)
- Warm-up: 5–10 min cardio + joint prep + ramp-up sets.
- Main lift(s): 3–5 sets compound, 5–10 reps, RIR 1–2 (occasionally 0–1 as specified).
- Secondary compounds: 3–4 sets, 6–12 reps.
- Accessories/isolation: 2–4 sets, 10–20 reps.
- Cooldown: light cardio 3–5 min + stretching for trained muscles.

Notes on Exercise Selection/Substitution
- Swap as needed for equipment or joints while keeping pattern: squat pattern (back, hack, front), hinge (RDL, deadlift variant), horizontal press (bench/DB), vertical press (OHP/DB), horizontal pull (row), vertical pull (pull-up/pulldown), single-leg (split squat/lunge), hip thrust/bridge, curls/extensions/raises.
- If elbows/shoulders irritated: favor cables/DBs, neutral grips, and machine presses/rows.

Progression and Load Targets
- Compounds: aim to add 5–10 lb lower, 2.5–5 lb upper when hitting top reps on all sets with target RIR.
- Accessories: add 1–2 reps until top of range, then +2.5–5 lb.
- If a lift stalls 2–3 weeks, change variation next phase or use rep range shift (e.g., 8–10 to 10–12) and reset load ~5%.

Recovery and Monitoring
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours nightly.
- Steps: 6–10k/day for general recovery.
- Mobility: 5–8 min post-session for trained joints.
- RPE/RIR log: note pumps, performance, soreness. If systemic fatigue rises, pull 2–4 sets/week across plan for 1 week.

Basic Nutrition Guidelines for Hypertrophy
- Calories: 200–300 kcal/day surplus to start; adjust by scale trend (+0.25–0.5% bodyweight/week).
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day across 3–5 meals.
- Carbs: 3–6 g/kg/day; front-load around training.
- Fats: 0.6–1.0 g/kg/day.
- Pre-workout (60–120 min): 25–50 g protein + 40–80 g carbs.
- Post-workout (0–3 hrs): 25–50 g protein + 60–100 g carbs.
- Hydration: bodyweight(kg) x 30–40 ml water/day + 500–1000 ml per hour of training.
- Supplements (optional): creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day, caffeine 3–6 mg/kg pre if tolerated, vitamin D if deficient, whey or casein for convenience, electrolyte mix if sweating heavily.

Here’s a lean-mass gain nutrition plan to pair with the 12-week hypertrophy program. It targets steady weight gain (+0.25–0.5% bodyweight/week), high protein, ample carbs to fuel training, and smart peri-workout nutrition. Adjust numbers based on the client’s starting bodyweight and weekly scale trends.

Calorie targets and adjustments
- Starting surplus: +200–300 kcal/day above true maintenance.
- Expected gain: 0.25–0.5% bodyweight/week. If <0.2% for 2 weeks, add +100–150 kcal/day; if >0.6–0.7% for 2 weeks, subtract 100–150 kcal/day.
- Maintenance finder: track 7-day average weight and intake for 10–14 days; the intake that stabilizes weight is maintenance. Add the surplus to this number.
- Phase tweaks:
  - Weeks 1–3, 5–7, 9–12 (hard training): run full surplus.
  - Deload weeks 4 and 8: pull back 100–150 kcal/day (mostly from carbs).

Macro guidelines
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (or 0.7–1.0 g/lb). Distribute over 3–5 meals with 25–50 g protein each.
- Carbohydrate: 3–6 g/kg/day (higher end on leg days and high-volume weeks). Aim for 1.5–2x protein intake in grams at minimum.
- Fat: 0.6–0.9 g/kg/day. Keep at least 20–25% of total calories; adjust mainly via fats and carbs as needed.
- Fiber: 10–15 g per 1,000 kcal (usually 25–40 g/day), without crowding out calories.

Peri-workout nutrition
- Pre-workout (60–120 min prior):
  - 25–40 g protein (whey, Greek yogurt, lean meat)
  - 40–90 g low–moderate GI carbs (rice, oats, potatoes, fruit, bagel)
  - Optional: 5 g creatine; 3–6 mg/kg caffeine 30–60 min pre if tolerated.
- Intra (optional for >75–90 min or high-volume leg sessions):
  - 15–30 g easily digested carbs (cyclic dextrin, sports drink) + electrolytes.
- Post-workout (0–3 hours after):
  - 30–50 g protein
  - 60–120 g carbs (faster-digesting is fine: rice, cereal, fruit, chocolate milk)
  - Minimal fat immediately post to speed gastric emptying.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Daily water: 30–40 ml/kg bodyweight + 500–1000 ml per training hour.
- Sodium: 3–5 g/day (from salt and foods), higher if sweating heavily. Include potassium- and magnesium-rich foods (bananas, potatoes, leafy greens, yogurt, nuts).

Meal timing and distribution
- 4 meals/day template works well:
  - Breakfast
  - Lunch
  - Pre-workout snack or shake (60–120 min pre)
  - Dinner/Post-workout
- Protein evenly split; anchor carbs around training (50–60% of daily carbs pre/post).
- Last meal: include 30–40 g slow protein (casein, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese) + some carbs if total daily carbs are low.

Food quality and choices
- Protein: lean beef, chicken, turkey, whole eggs/egg whites, fish (salmon, tuna), Greek yogurt, skyr, cottage cheese, whey/casein, tofu/tempeh/edamame.
- Carbs: rice, oats, potatoes, sweet potatoes, pasta, quinoa, whole-grain breads, fruit, low-fat dairy, cereals. Use some refined carbs around workouts if appetite is an issue.
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts/nut butters, whole eggs, fatty fish, dark chocolate (in moderation).
- Vegetables: 2–4 servings/day for micros and fiber; don’t let veg volume suppress appetite excessively.

Sample calorie/macro setups by bodyweight
- 70 kg (154 lb): Maintenance ~2,400–2,600 kcal. Start 2,700–2,900 kcal.
  - Protein 140–160 g, Carbs 330–420 g, Fat 65–80 g.
- 80 kg (176 lb): Maintenance ~2,700–2,900 kcal. Start 3,000–3,200 kcal.
  - Protein 160–180 g, Carbs 360–460 g, Fat 75–90 g.
- 90 kg (198 lb): Maintenance ~3,000–3,200 kcal. Start 3,300–3,500 kcal.
  - Protein 180–200 g, Carbs 400–500 g, Fat 80–100 g.
Adjust to the individual’s real maintenance and activity—these are starting points.

Two sample day menus (swap items to taste)

Sample Day A (training day ~3,100 kcal; ~180 P / 430 C / 80 F)
- Breakfast: 3 whole eggs + 200 g egg whites scrambled, 100 g oats cooked with 1 banana and honey; 250 ml orange juice.
- Lunch: 180 g chicken breast, 250 g cooked jasmine rice, 1 cup mixed veg, 1 tbsp olive oil.
- Pre-workout: Greek yogurt (200 g) + granola (60 g) + berries; 5 g creatine.
- Post-workout/Dinner: 200 g lean beef, 300 g cooked potatoes, asparagus; 1 bagel with jam.

Sample Day B (rest/deload ~2,900 kcal; ~180 P / 350 C / 90 F)
- Breakfast: Protein smoothie (40 g whey, 300 ml milk, oats 60 g, berries, 1 tbsp flaxseed).
- Lunch: 180 g salmon, 220 g cooked rice, salad with olive oil/lemon.
- Snack: Turkey sandwich (120 g turkey, whole-grain bread x2, slice cheese) + fruit.

- Evening: Greek yogurt (250 g) + granola (40 g) + dark chocolate (20 g).

Supplements (optional, evidence-based)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily, any time.
- Caffeine: 3–6 mg/kg pre-workout if tolerated.
- Whey/casein: to help hit protein targets.
- Vitamin D3: 1,000–2,000 IU/day if bloodwork or low sun exposure suggests.
- Omega-3s: 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if oily fish intake is low.
- Electrolytes: add sodium/potassium/magnesium on hot, sweaty sessions.

Monitoring and adherence
- Weigh 3–4 mornings/week (after bathroom, before food); track 7-day average.
- Goal: gain 0.25–0.5%/week. Adjust calories in 100–150 kcal steps.
- Track performance: if lifts stagnate and weight stable, add carbs first (+25–50 g/day).
- Appetite management: use more liquid calories, lower-fiber carb sources, and condiments if struggling to eat; increase veg volume and lean proteins if gaining too fast.
- Alcohol: minimal during the block; if included, keep to 0–2 drinks/week max.

- Weeks 1–3, 5–7, 9–12: full surplus, higher carb days on Legs and Pull.
- Weeks 4 and 8 deloads: pull ~100–150 kcal/day (mostly carbs), keep protein constant, keep hydration/micros high.

Below are two weekly conditioning sessions designed to complement the 12-week hypertrophy plan without compromising gains. They prioritize aerobic base, recovery, and a small dose of high-intensity work for work capacity and cardiovascular health. Place them on rest days or after shorter upper sessions. Keep total weekly strength performance the priority—if recovery dips, scale conditioning volume first.

General rules
- Frequency: 2 sessions/week throughout all 12 weeks.
- Order: Preferably separate from heavy lower-body lifting by 24 hours. If same day, do conditioning after lifting.
- Progression: Build duration/intensity gradually; deload in Weeks 4 and 8 alongside lifting deloads.
- Effort scales: Use RPE (0–10) or %HRmax. Nasal-breathing “conversational” pace = Zone 2 (~60–70% HRmax, RPE 5–6).
- Footstrike variety: Use low-impact modalities (bike, rower, incline walk) to save joints and quads for lifting.

Session templates by phase

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Aerobic base + technique
- Goal: Build aerobic capacity, aid recovery, minimal interference.

Session A: Zone 2 steady state
- Modality: Bike or incline treadmill walk (5–8% incline).
- Week 1: 25 min @ Zone 2 + 5 min easy cool-down.
- Week 2: 30 min @ Zone 2 + 5 min cool-down.
- Week 3: 35 min @ Zone 2 + 5 min cool-down.
- Week 4 (deload): 20–25 min @ Zone 2 + 5 min cool-down.
- Cadence: Smooth, steady breathing; can speak in sentences.
- Optional finisher: 3 x 20–30 s very light strides or fast spins, RPE 6, full recovery—only if you feel fresh.

Session B: Aerobic intervals (extensive)
- Modality: Rower, assault/air bike, or elliptical.
- Week 1: 6 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7, 1 min easy between. 5 min warm-up/cool-down.
- Week 2: 7 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7, 1 min easy.
- Week 3: 8 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7, 1 min easy.
- Week 4 (deload): 5 x 2 min @ RPE 6, 1 min easy.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Maintain base + introduce brief intensity
- Goal: Slightly higher intensity without excessive eccentric load.

Session A: Tempo/threshold intervals
- Modality: Bike or rower.
- Warm-up: 6–8 min easy + 3 x 20 s pickups.
- Week 5: 3 x 6 min @ upper Zone 3 (RPE 7), 2 min easy between.
- Week 6: 3 x 7 min @ RPE 7, 2 min easy.
- Week 7: 4 x 6 min @ RPE 7, 2 min easy.
- Week 8 (deload): 2 x 6–7 min @ RPE 6–7, 2 min easy. Keep total time reduced ~40–50%.

Session B: Low-impact HIIT (short sprints)
- Modality: Air bike or rower (avoid hard running sprints to spare joints).
- Warm-up: 8–10 min easy + 3 x 10 s fast spins.
- Protocol: 8–10 rounds of 15 s hard (RPE 9) / 45 s easy.
- Progression: 
  - Week 5: 8 rounds
  - Week 6: 9 rounds
  - Week 7: 10 rounds
  - Week 8 (deload): 6–8 rounds at RPE 8–9
- Cool-down: 5 min easy.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Sharpen work capacity, keep interference low
- Goal: Maintain cardio with one quality session and one recovery-focused session.

Session A: Mixed-modal aerobic circuit (continuous)
- 30–40 min continuous at Zone 2–low Zone 3 (RPE 6–7), rotate every 5 min between:
  - Bike
  - Rower
  - Incline walk or sled push (light)
- Week 9: 30 min; Week 10: 35 min; Week 11: 40 min; Week 12: 35–40 min (hold or slightly pull back if fatigue rises).
- Keep cadence smooth, no grinding.

Session B: Sprint-lite or fartlek
- Modality: Air bike, rower, or soft-tissue-friendly jog/fartlek on turf/track.
- Warm-up: 8–10 min easy + drills.
- Protocol (progressive fartlek):
  - Week 9: 8 cycles of 30 s fast (RPE 8–9) / 90 s easy.
  - Week 10: 10 cycles of 30 s fast / 90 s easy.
  - Week 11: 8 cycles of 45 s fast / 75 s easy.
  - Week 12: 6–8 cycles of 45 s fast / 75 s easy, cap RPE at 8–9.
- Cool-down: 5–8 min easy.

Placement suggestions across the 5-day lift split
- Example week (Phase 1 U/L/U/L + optional pump):
  - Mon: Upper A
  - Tue: Conditioning A (Zone 2)
  - Wed: Lower A
  - Thu: Upper B
  - Fri: Conditioning B (intervals)
  - Sat: Lower B (+ optional pump if recovery is great; if so, keep conditioning B on Fri light)
  - Sun: Rest
- For PPL + U/L phases, place Zone 2 after Push or Upper; place HIIT 24 h away from heavy Legs.

Volume management and interference prevention
- Keep HIIT bike/rower dominant to reduce eccentric stress.
- If lower-body DOMS or squat/RDL performance dips, reduce HIIT rounds by 2–3 or swap to Zone 2 that week.
- If resting heart rate rises >5–7 bpm above baseline or sleep tanks, cut one session by 50% duration that week.

Optional add-ons
- Sled pushes: 6–10 x 20–30 m light-moderate, RPE 6–7, 60–90 s rest (can replace any Session B once per week).
- Loaded carries finisher (post-upper): 4–6 x 30–40 m farmer carries at RPE 7, 60–90 s rest. Counts toward conditioning if time-crunched.

Peri-conditioning fuel
- Easy Zone 2 <45 min: water + electrolytes; small carb snack if desired.
- Intervals/HIIT: 20–40 g carbs 30–60 min prior; optional 10–20 g during if >40 min total.
- Post: prioritize carbs/protein similar to lifting days.

This structure keeps conditioning supportive of hypertrophy, improves recovery and work capacity, and won’t hijack leg growth when managed as above. Adjust intensity/duration down first if weekly lifting performance suffers.

Got it. Here’s a focused, hotel-gym-friendly plan for Weeks 5–6 that preserves hypertrophy stimulus using dumbbells, bands/bodyweight, and minimal equipment. It slots directly into the 12-week block, replacing Week 5–6 sessions. We’ll keep frequency at 5 lifts/week plus 2 conditioning sessions (tweaked for travel), maintain weekly set targets, and emphasize close proximity to failure with slower eccentrics, long ranges of motion, and strategic intensifiers.

Guiding principles for Weeks 5–6 (travel)
- Equipment: Dumbbells, adjustable bench, floor, bands (if available), towel. No barbell/machines.
- Split: Push / Pull / Legs / Upper / Lower (5 days). Two conditioning sessions.
- Loading: Choose the heaviest DBs you can handle with good form. Take most working sets to RIR 0–2. Use tempo (3–4s eccentrics), 1–2s pauses in stretched positions, and extended sets (partials, myo-reps, drop sets if lighter DBs).
- Volume: 12–16 sets per large muscle group/week. If DBs are very light, add 1–2 sets and/or intensifiers.

Week 6

  - Add 1–2 reps per set within ranges.

Week 5–6 conditioning (hotel-friendly)

Here is the full 12-week hypertrophy program incorporating the two-week hotel-gym travel block (Weeks 5–6) and the return-to-gym re-entry and deload (Week 7 re-entry, Week 8 deload), followed by the original Phase 3 push. It includes phases, week-by-week structure, days, exercises, sets/reps, and key notes.

Global training guidelines
- Frequency: 5 lifting days/week + 2 conditioning sessions/week
- Intensity: Work mostly at 1–3 RIR; compounds occasionally 0–1 RIR as specified
- Tempo: 2–3 s eccentric (3–4 s during travel block), controlled concentric
- Rest: 2–3 min compounds; 60–90 s accessories
- Warm-up: 5–10 min light cardio + dynamic mobility + 2–3 ramp sets for first two lifts
- Progression: Add reps to the top of the range, then add load (upper +2.5–5 lb; lower +5–10 lb)
- Deloads: Week 8; lighter intent in Week 7 re-entry

Phase 1: Foundation Volume and Technique (Weeks 1–4) — Upper/Lower x2 + optional pump
- Weekly target sets (wk1): quads 12–14; hams 10–12; glutes 10–12; chest 12–14; back 14–16; delts 10–12; biceps 8–10; triceps 8–10; calves 8–10; abs 6–8
- Progression: Weeks 1–3 add ~1 set per muscle group across the week; Week 4 deload

Week 1
Upper A
- Barbell bench press 4x6–8 (RIR 2)
- One-arm chest-supported row 4x8–10
- Incline DB press 3x8–10
- Lat pulldown (neutral) 3x10–12
- Seated DB lateral raise 3x12–15
- Cable fly or pec deck 2x12–15
- Rope triceps pressdown 3x10–12
- EZ-bar curl 3x10–12

Lower A
- Back squat 4x6–8
- Romanian deadlift 4x8–10
- Walking DB lunge 3x10–12/leg
- Seated/lying leg curl 3x10–12
- Leg extension 2x12–15
- Standing calf raise 4x8–12
- Hanging knee raise 3x12–15

Upper B
- Overhead press (BB/DB) 4x6–8
- Weighted pull-up or assisted 4x6–8
- Flat DB press 3x8–10
- Chest-supported T-bar row 3x8–10
- Cable lateral raise 3x12–15
- Rear delt cable fly 3x12–15
- Close-grip bench or dips 3x6–10
- Incline DB curl 3x10–12

Lower B
- Front squat or hack squat 4x6–8
- Hip thrust 4x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat 3x8–10/leg
- Leg curl (hip hinge emphasis) 3x10–12
- Leg extension 2x12–15
- Seated calf raise 4x10–15
- Pallof press 3x12–15/side

Optional Pump Day (if recovery is good)
- Lateral raise 4x15–20
- Cable curl 4x12–15
- Rope pressdown 4x12–15
- Rear delt fly 3x15–20 (RIR 2–3)

Week 2
- Same exercises; +1–2 reps or small load bumps. Add 1 set to a primary compound for chest, back, and quads if recovery is good.

Week 3
- Same menu; add 1 set to lagging areas. Last set of first two compounds per session may be pushed to RIR 0–1.

Week 4 (Deload)
- Reduce sets by ~50–60%, loads -10–15% from Week 3, keep RIR 3–4. No failure.

Phase 2A: Travel Block (Weeks 5–6) — Dumbbells/Bodyweight Only, P/P/L/U/L
- Goal: Maintain hypertrophy with high effort, long ROM, slow eccentrics, unilateral work
- Effort: Most sets to RIR 0–2; final set of 1–2 accessories can go to 0 RIR with a simple intensifier
- Tempo: 3–4 s eccentric, 1 s stretch pause where useful

Week 5

Push
- DB bench or floor press 4x8–12 (3s down, 1s pause) RIR 1–2
- Push-up (feet elevated if strong) 3xAMRAP to 0–1 RIR; last set rest-pause 15–20s
- DB incline press 3x10–15 (slow eccentric)
- DB overhead press 4x6–10
- DB lateral raise 4x12–20 (last set drop or partials)
- Overhead DB triceps extension 3x10–15

Pull
- 1-arm DB row 4x8–12/side (2s squeeze)
- DB Romanian deadlift 4x8–12 (3–4s down, pause near floor)
- Chest-supported rear delt raise 3x12–20
- DB pullover 3x10–15
- DB curl 3x10–15
- Hammer curl 2–3x10–15 (last set myo-reps: 12–15 + 20s + 4–5 + 20s + 3–4)

Legs
- Bulgarian split squat 4x8–12/leg (3s down, 1s pause) RIR 0–1
- DB RDL 4x8–12 (stretch focus)
- Goblet squat 4x10–15; 1.5 reps if load is light
- Reverse lunge 3x10–12/leg
- DB hip thrust or single-leg bridge 3x12–15 (2s top hold)
- Single-leg calf raise 4x10–15/leg (2s at top)

Upper (mixed)
- Neutral-grip DB overhead press 3x8–12
- 1-arm DB row 3x10–12/side
- DB incline press 3x8–12
- Chest-supported DB row (rear-delt bias) 3x12–15
- DB lateral raise 3x12–20 superset DB rear delt fly 3x12–20
- DB skull crusher or overhead triceps 2–3x10–15 superset DB curl 2–3x10–15

Lower + Core
- Heel-elevated DB squat 4x10–15 (3s down, 1s pause)
- DB RDL 3x8–12 (heavier/slower than earlier in week)
- Walking lunge 3x10–12/leg
- DB stiff-leg hinge to calf raise combo 3x12–15
- Copenhagen side plank 2–3x20–30s/side
- Hollow hold or dead bug 3x30–45s

Week 6
- Same exercise menu. Progress by adding 1–2 reps per set, adding a 4th set on 2–3 key moves/session, increasing eccentric to 4s with 1s stretch pause, and/or using one intensifier on 1–2 accessories per workout. Increase DB load if available and reps are capped.

Travel conditioning (Weeks 5–6)
- Session A (Zone 2): 25–35 min incline walk/bike/row/jog at conversational pace; 3–5 min warm-up/cool-down
- Session B (Intervals): 8–10 rounds of 30 s hard (RPE 8–9) / 60 s easy; 8 min warm-up, 5 min cool-down. In Week 6, add 1–2 rounds or slight resistance bump
- Place after Push/Upper or on non-leg days, ~24 h from hard leg work

Phase 2B: Re-entry and Consolidation (Weeks 7–8)
- Week 7: Re-entry to barbells/machines at submax loads, RIR 2–3 on main lifts, normal volume but no intensifiers
- Week 8: Formal deload (as originally planned)

Week 7 (Re-entry, P/P/L/U/L)

Push
- Barbell bench press 4x6–8 @ RIR 2–3 (about 90% of pre-travel load)
- Incline DB press 3x8–10 @ RIR 1–2
- Seated DB shoulder press 3x8–10
- Cable fly (low-to-high) 3x12–15
- Lateral raise 3x12–20
- Overhead cable triceps extension 3x10–12
- Optional dips 2x8–12 @ RIR 2

Pull
- Weighted pull-up or pulldown 4x6–8 @ RIR 2–3
- Chest-supported row 4x8–10 @ RIR 1–2
- Single-arm lat cable pulldown 3x10–12/side
- Reverse pec deck 3x12–15
- Barbell/EZ-bar curl 3x8–10
- Incline DB hammer curl 2x10–12
- Face pull 2x15–20

Legs
- Hack squat or high-bar squat 4x6–8 @ RIR 2–3 (1 s pause in hole on first 2 sets)
- Romanian deadlift 3–4x8–10 @ RIR 2
- Leg press 3x10–12
- Seated leg curl 3x10–12
- Walking lunge 2x12/leg (light)
- Standing calf raise 4x8–12
- Ab wheel 3x10–12

Upper
- Overhead press 4x6–8 @ RIR 2–3
- Flat DB press 3x8–10
- T-bar or cable row 3x8–10
- Neutral-grip pulldown 3x10–12
- Cable lateral raise 3x12–15
- Skull crushers 2x10–12
- Cable curl 2x10–12

Lower
- Front squat 4x5–7 @ RIR 2–3
- Hip thrust 4x8–10
- Leg curl 3x10–12
- Leg extension 3x12–15
- Seated calf raise 4x10–15
- Hanging leg raise 3x12–15

Week 8 (Deload, same P/P/L/U/L structure)
- Reduce total sets by 50–60%
- Loads -10–15% from Week 7 or maintain loads but stop far from failure (RIR 3–4)
- No intensifiers, crisp technique
- Conditioning: Zone 2 and light intervals only (RPE 6–7)

Phase 3: Advanced Hypertrophy (Weeks 9–12) — Upper / Lower / Push / Pull / Legs
- Strategy: Rebuild to and surpass pre-travel loads by Week 10; strategic intensifiers on 1 accessory per session in Week 9–10, up to 1–2 in Weeks 11–12; top set + back-off structure reintroduced

Week 9

Upper
- Barbell bench press 4x6–8 (RIR 1–2)
- Weighted pull-up 4x6–8
- Incline DB press 3x8–10
- Chest-supported row 3x8–10
- Cable lateral raise 3x12–15 (last set drop 25% then 6–8)
- Rope pressdown 3x10–12
- EZ-bar curl 3x10–12

Lower
- Back squat 4x5–7 (RIR 1–2)
- RDL 4x6–8 (slightly heavier; RIR 1–2)
- Leg press 3x10–12 (close-stance quad bias)
- Seated leg curl 3x10–12
- Standing calf raise 4x8–12
- Decline sit-up 3x10–15

Push
- Incline barbell press 4x6–8
- Seated DB shoulder press 3x8–10
- Cable fly 3x12–15
- Lateral raise 3x12–20 (rest-pause on last set: 12–15 + 15s + 5–6)
- Overhead cable triceps extension 3x10–12
- Dips 2x8–12

Pull
- Chest-supported row 4x6–8
- Neutral-grip pulldown 3x8–10
- Single-arm cable row 3x10–12/side
- Reverse pec deck 3x12–15
- Barbell curl 3x8–10
- Incline hammer curl 2x10–12
- Face pull 2x15–20

Legs
- Hack squat 4x6–8
- Hip thrust 4x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat 3x8–10/leg
- Leg curl 3x10–12
- Leg extension 2x12–15 (last set drop 25% then 8–10)
- Seated calf raise 4x10–15
- Ab wheel 3x10–12

Week 10
- Compounds: progress to ~95–100% of best pre-travel loads, RIR 1–2
- First compound each session: top set within range at RIR 0–1 if ready, then 1–2 back-offs at -8–12% load for 1–2 more reps
- Add 1 extra set across 2–3 lagging muscles this week (+2–4 total weekly sets)
- Keep intensifiers capped at 1 accessory per day

Week 11
- First compound each day: top set RIR 0–1 within range, then 2 back-offs @ RIR 1–2
- Accessories: 1 movement/day with a single intensifier (drop or rest-pause)
- Maintain volume unless recovery is excellent

Week 12
- Controlled overreach: same volume as Week 11
- Compounds: keep back-offs at RIR ~1–2; avoid ugly grinders
- Accessories: 1–2 movements/session may go to failure with one drop or brief rest-pause
- After Week 12: take 3–5 easy days or a light deload before next block

Conditioning across all 12 weeks (adjusted around travel/re-entry)
- Two sessions per week
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): 
  - Session A: Zone 2 steady 25–35 min
  - Session B: Extensive intervals 6–8 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7, 1 min easy
- Week 4 (Deload): Cut duration/rounds by ~40–50%
- Weeks 5–6 (Travel): 
  - Session A: Zone 2 25–35 min
  - Session B: 8–10 x 30 s hard / 60 s easy (RPE 8–9)
- Week 7 (Re-entry): 
  - Session A: Zone 2, 25–35 min @ RPE 5–6
  - Session B: 6–8 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7, 1 min easy
- Week 8 (Deload): Easy Zone 2 + light intervals (RPE 6–7), reduce volume ~40–50%
- Weeks 9–12:
  - Session A: Mixed-modal Zone 2–low 3, 30–40 min (rotate bike/row/walk/sled)
  - Session B: Intervals 8–10 x 30 s fast / 60–90 s easy @ RPE 8–9
- Placement: Prefer after Push/Upper or on rest days; keep ~24 h from heavy Legs

Lean-mass nutrition (summary)
- Surplus: +200–300 kcal/day above maintenance; target +0.25–0.5% BW/week
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day across 3–5 meals
- Carbs: 3–6 g/kg/day; bias around training
- Fats: 0.6–0.9 g/kg/day
- Deload Weeks 4 and 8: pull 100–150 kcal/day (carbs), maintain protein
- Peri-workout: 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs pre; 30–50 g protein + 60–100 g carbs post
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day + 500–1000 ml per training hour
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/d, caffeine pre (3–6 mg/kg), whey/casein, vitamin D3 if needed, omega-3s if fish intake is low

Key coaching notes
- Prioritize proximity to failure over absolute load in the travel block using tempo, ROM, unilateral work, and simple intensifiers
- Week 7 is about re-grooving positions and restoring tissue tolerance; cap at RIR 2–3 on compounds
- Week 8 deload consolidates before the final push
- Weeks 9–12: re-establish pre-travel loads by Week 10; push top sets and targeted intensification Weeks 11–12
- Auto-regulate: if systemic fatigue or joint irritation rises, first remove intensifiers, then reduce total weekly sets by 10–20% for 7 days

This revised 12-week plan preserves hypertrophy through travel, safely reintroduces heavy loading, and finishes with a strong progressive push. Adjust small load/reps week to week based on performance and recovery.
